items.s: Many people feel ____ when they talk about money with a partner, so they avoid it.

match.d: things you own, such as a house or land
the legal end of a marriage

items.s: The Guardian ____ on this on 11 November 2026.
A recent Harris Poll ____ that 53% of people had signed a prenup.

Some people ____ the idea uncomfortable.
My cousin ____ a prenup before he got married last year.

tfn.s: The poll found that 53% of married or engaged Americans under 45 had signed a prenup.
tfn.why: The text says: "53% of married or engaged Americans under 45 said they had signed a prenup"

tfn.s: A prenup is only for very rich people.
tfn.why: The text says: "the idea is no longer only for very rich people"

tfn.s: The text says how much a prenup costs.
tfn.why: The text does not say how much a prenup costs.

tfn.s: Some couples say that talking honestly about money helps them feel closer.
tfn.why: The text says: "Some couples say honesty about money brings them closer."

tfn.s: The writer thinks every couple should sign a prenup.
tfn.why: The text says: "The important part of the story is not that everyone should rush out and sign a contract."

pre.d: made or agreed before two people get married
people who like an idea and say it is good

the ability to decide things or to control others

focus.note: A collocation is a pair of words that people often use together. Learn the whole pair, such as 'make a decision', not just one word.

match.d: something that keeps you safe from harm

items.s: A Guardian feature ____ on 11 November 2026.
By the time they married, the couple ____ a prenup.
The conversation may ____ uncomfortable if one partner earns far more than the other.
If someone you loved ____ you to sign one, would you agree?
Legal arrangements ____ between countries.

tfn.s: Some young Americans think of a prenup as protection, not as a prediction that the marriage will fail.
tfn.why: The text says they see prenups "as a form of protection rather than a prediction of failure"

tfn.s: The writer believes the poll shows that most young couples everywhere sign prenups.
tfn.why: The text says: "That does not prove that most young couples everywhere are following the trend."

tfn.s: Most couples who sign a prenup later use it in court.
tfn.why: The text does not say how often prenups are used in court.

tfn.s: An agreement that looks fair at the start may stop being fair later.
tfn.why: The text says: "A contract that appears fair today might look very different after years of childcare, career sacrifices or unexpected illness."

tfn.s: The writer says courts everywhere treat prenups in the same way.
tfn.why: The text says: "its treatment by courts depends on local law and individual circumstances"

pre.d: a serious promise to stay with someone or do something
the way you think and feel about something
slowly changing
to have enough money to pay for something
people who say what is wrong with something
rude and likely to upset someone
a change that more and more people follow
not needed

focus.note: Check the whole phrase, not just one word. If a word sounds odd with its partner, it is probably wrong, even when the meaning is close.

items.s: The couple tried to ____ an agreement that felt fair to both of them.
One partner may step back from work to ____ children.
If one partner wants to ____ a family business, an agreement can protect it.
Money can lead to a ____ argument, even between people who love each other.
Some couples keep a ____ bank account for bills.
A survey of students and one of retirees are hardly ____, whatever the headline says.
Some people feel that planning for separation ____ the commitment itself.
A solicitor may ____ a settlement on behalf of a client who dislikes conflict.
While one partner stays at home, the other keeps ____ wealth.
The judge ordered full ____ of both partners' assets before the hearing.
Trust may grow when couples can talk ____ about worrying possibilities.

match.d: how far a court can make people obey an agreement
the state of being open to being hurt
areas or countries that have their own laws

items.s: Prenups are no longer confined to ____ families.
Younger Americans show a growing ____ to confront the question.
Couples need ____ about what financial fairness means to each of them.
The contract looked fair at first, but its long-term effects were deeply ____.

tfn.s: The writer treats the 53% figure as suggestive rather than conclusive.
tfn.why: The text says the numbers "should not be treated as a precise measure of a universal trend, but they help explain" the discussion.

tfn.s: The text argues that a signed prenup guarantees fair treatment for the partner who earns less.
tfn.why: The text says the idea that a contract "automatically protects both people deserves scrutiny".

tfn.s: Most couples who sign a prenup have been married before.
tfn.why: The text does not say whether the couples have been married before.

tfn.s: A partner who leaves a career to raise children could end up worse off under an agreement made before the wedding.
tfn.why: The text says an arrangement that seemed reasonable could later feel "profoundly unequal" after one partner steps away from a career.

tfn.s: The text says that independent advice alone makes every prenup enforceable.
tfn.why: The text says enforceability "may depend on disclosure, independent advice and whether the terms are considered fair", so advice is not enough.

things of value that a person owns, such as money and property
easily broken or damaged
people who publicly support an idea
things you believe are true without checking
good for you and likely to help you
impossible to change back
very strongly or deeply

focus.note: Advanced writers choose precise pairs. Learn the verb or adjective together with its noun, because a near synonym often sounds wrong.

speak.title: Role-play: should we sign a prenup?
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.role: the partner who wants a prenup
a.text: You own a small business and have savings from your grandparents. You'd like a prenup before the wedding. Explain why it isn't a sign that you don't love your partner.

b.text: Planning for a divorce before the wedding feels cold to you. Ask why your partner wants a prenup, say how you feel, and try to find a deal you both like.

phrases: I'd like to talk about money before the wedding.
I'm not saying we don't trust each other.
It doesn't feel very romantic to me.
What if we got advice from a lawyer first?
That's a fair point, but I'm still worried.
Could we agree on something we're both happy with?
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did you agree to sign a prenup, and what did you decide to include?
